resources.string: Detects when the on-screen keyboard opens and places your chosen privacy shade above it. VeilType does not read, store, or transmit screen or typed content.
Hide control until the keyboard reopens
Open a keyboard to use the veil, or cover the whole screen.
A little privacy, wherever you type.
Let your apps do the remembering.
A small control appears with your keyboard. Tap it to cover the screen above your keys.
Touch and hold the veil to see underneath; release to cover it again. You can also let touches pass through.
Choose apps to veil automatically, skip, or cover completely. Your choices stay on this device.
Set up the veil once, then bring it up whenever you need a little space.
Lets VeilType place the cover and control above other apps.
Detects the keyboard and foreground app without reading their content.
Provides controls while VeilType is armed.
Open a keyboard to find the control.
Runs quietly until you need it.
The service is stopped. Turn it on again when access is ready.
Arm the veil, tap the field, then use the control on your keyboard.

VeilType works offline. Accessibility access observes keyboard window bounds and the foreground app for your rules. It never reads screen or typed text. Preferences, app rules and your chosen photo reference stay on this device. A veil is a visual aid, not protection against screenshots or cameras.
If the control does not appear, check both access settings and your device’s background restrictions.
Adjust the veil, its control, and where it appears.
Touches pass through; hold the control to peek. On Android 12 and later, opacity is limited to 80%% in this mode.
Choose one rule for each app. Manual screen cover remains available independently.
Cover the screen when a keyboard opens unless an app has a different rule.
Limit automatic rules to the days and times you choose. Manual controls still work.
An overnight period belongs to the day it starts.
Equal start and end times mean all day.
Restore the armed service after your device restarts.
VeilType observes top-level window types and bounds to find the keyboard, and the foreground app name to apply your app rules. A separate display-over-apps permission lets it draw the veil.

VeilType does not read screen content, typed text, passwords, clipboard data or screenshots. Your settings, app rules and selected photo reference stay on this device. VeilType has no internet permission.
Android will show a broad warning because accessibility access is powerful. You can revoke it in Settings at any time.
I understand and choose to enable this access.
